title: DOWN THE TOXICITY RABBIT HOLE: A NOVEL FRAMEWORK TO BIAS AUDIT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Iteratively prompting LLMs to generate increasingly toxic text starting from religious stereotypes (e.g., Islam, Judaism), and analyzing the outputs using FastText word embeddings (nearest neighbors) and measuring the presence of necessity modals implying violence.

Applying the 'toxicity rabbit hole' framework to hundreds of ethnic identity groups, evaluating the frequency of targeted slurs, calls for ethnic cleansing via necessity modals, and safety filter compliance.

Iteratively eliciting toxic content targeting 193 nationalities and analyzing unigram distribution disparities between continents to identify specific geographic biases and themes in the generated text.

Generating iterative toxic expansions targeting women and feminists, and analyzing the resulting text via FastText word embedding nearest neighbors to identify misogynistic associations and safety evaluation failures.

bias_targets.target: Sexual orientation and Gender identity bias
bias_targets.methodology: Using the iterative toxicity framework on LGBTQ+ identity groups and analyzing the generated text for homophobic and transphobic content, including evaluating the frequency of specific slurs.
Applying the iterative toxic generation framework to disabled identity groups and analyzing the nearest neighbors in trained word embeddings for ableist associations and harmful stereotypes.

Eliciting toxic continuations starting from stereotypes about political affiliations (e.g., Democrats, Republicans, Liberals) to evaluate the amplification of political schisms and generation of hyper-partisan text.
